design_decisions.made_in_response_to: disclosed limitation, surfaced after first full pipeline run - NOT the original design
design_decisions.rationale: Agent 3's routing, forced by Agent 2's inflow estimates, tops out at ~78% simulated fill across all lead times - far below the CONFIRMED real peak (159%). Absolute fill/outflow thresholds calibrated to real capacity therefore never fire and would not be a fair test of the pipeline's timing behavior. Two disclosed factors contribute to that ~15x inflow-magnitude gap: (1) Agent 2's rainfall-runoff transform (SCS-CN + single-tank routing) is an uncalibrated, planning-level approximation - no basin-specific hydrograph data was available to fit it; (2) the forcing data itself: this project independently confirmed gfs_seamless underestimates observed rainfall at this site - for 2026-02-04, the D0 forecast was 20.9mm vs. 49.9mm actually observed (ERA5, archive-api), i.e. the forecast captured roughly 42% of the observed total. See data/raw/daily_comparison_loukkos_jan-feb2026.csv. Given both factors, Agent 4 adopted rate-of-rise (inflow vs. its own trailing 3-day mean) as the PRIMARY elevated-risk signal - scale-independent, and standard real-world flood early-warning practice for exactly this situation. Absolute-threshold rules are still computed and logged every run for transparency (see agent4_risk / agent5_regulatory below) even though they currently show 0 crossings.

D0.rationale:
Rationale text below — normal prose, since it's a work product, not chat filler.

---

**D0 Forecast Rationale — Oued El Makhazine, valid window early Feb 2026 crisis**

At this lead time (D0), the pipeline's DERIVED simulation projected a peak inflow of 205.7 m3/s on 2026-02-07, driving reservoir fill to a simulated peak of 73.9% of nominal capacity (672.9 Mm3, CONFIRMED). Both anticipatory and reactive release policies converged on the same simulated peak outflow of 5.0 m3/s, so the pipeline found no differentiating benefit between the two strategies at this lead time. Agent 4 flagged elevated rate-of-rise risk as early as 2026-01-24 (0-day lead), based on a DERIVED estimate of 520.37x baseline inflow. Agent 5 recorded zero regulatory constraint violations in this DERIVED simulation run. Note that these DERIVED figures are a simplified estimate and diverge sharply from the CONFIRMED real event: official/press-sourced data show real peak inflow reached 3210 m3/s (2026-01-28), real peak fill hit 166.4% (2026-02-10), and real peak controlled outflow reached 878 m3/s (2026-02-09) — none of which the D0 simulation anticipated.

numeric_summary.first_flag_summary: first triggered for valid-date 2026-01-24 (520.37x baseline inflow), information available on 2026-01-24 (0d lead)

T-24h.rationale: DERIVED simulation (T-24h lead, illustrative only): peak inflow 171.6 m³/s on 2026-02-07, reservoir fill peaking at 68.4% of nominal capacity, anticipatory and reactive outflow policies converging on same 5.0 m³/s peak release. Agent 4 flagged elevated rate-of-rise risk 1 day ahead of the 2026-01-23 valid date (200.23x baseline inflow spike). Agent 5 found 0 regulatory constraint violations across the run, so no policy override needed at this lead time. For context only, CONFIRMED official figures show a much larger real event (peak fill 166.4% on 2026-02-10, peak inflow 3210 m³/s on 2026-01-28, peak controlled outflow 878 m³/s on 2026-02-09) — these are NOT what this T-24h simulation produced, and shouldn't be merged with the DERIVED numbers above.

numeric_summary.first_flag_summary: first triggered for valid-date 2026-01-23 (200.23x baseline inflow), information available on 2026-01-22 (1d lead)

T-48h.rationale:
T-48h forecast (2026-01-23 → valid 2026-01-25): DERIVED sim show elevated-risk flag first trigger, inflow 4.78x baseline. Pipeline sim (illustrative, not real event) project peak inflow 187.9 m3/s (2026-02-04), reservoir fill peak 72.4% nominal capacity. Anticipatory vs reactive outflow policy tie, both 5.0 m3/s — no differentiation this lead time. Agent 5 found 0 regulatory violations across sim.

Note: CONFIRMED real event far exceed these DERIVED numbers — real peak inflow 3210 m3/s (2026-01-28), real fill 166.4% nominal (2026-02-10), real controlled outflow 878 m3/s (2026-02-09). DERIVED sim badly undercount actual crisis magnitude — treat as illustrative pipeline output only, not forecast of real event.

T-72h.rationale: At T-72h lead time, DERIVED simulation flagged elevated risk early: rate-of-rise flag first tripped for valid-date 2026-01-24 (16.29x baseline inflow), with that signal available 3 days ahead on 2026-01-21. Simulated peak inflow reached 358.0 m³/s (2026-02-04), driving reservoir fill to 78.2% of nominal capacity — no regulatory constraint violations recorded (0 rows). Anticipatory and reactive outflow policies converged to same simulated peak, 5.0 m3/s, no differentiation benefit shown at this lead time. For context only — CONFIRMED official record shows real event far exceeded these derived numbers: real peak inflow 3210 m3/s (2026-01-28), real peak fill 166.4% (2026-02-10), real peak controlled outflow 878 m3/s (2026-02-09). Do not blend: DERIVED figures are this pipeline's simplified estimate at T-72h, not a match to CONFIRMED real event magnitude.
